text:
The air in the dining room was thick, heavy with the weight of unspoken words. Emily slid into her chair, the wood scraping softly against the floor, a sound that seemed deafening in the quiet. She kept her gaze fixed on the centerpiece, a vase of wilting lilies, afraid to look up at the faces that had raised her. Her father’s voice cut through the stillness, warm but edged with steel. "We understand it's been hard, and we're not here to judge, only to support," he said. His tone was a balm, yet his jaw remained set, a silent testament to the expectations that loomed over them all.

In the corner of the room, perched on a high shelf, sat a porcelain figurine of a giraffe. It was the animal known for its long neck, a creature that had to crane its head high just to see the horizon. Like the giraffe, Emily felt the strain of looking up, of trying to see a future that felt just out of reach, while her family watched from below, their eyes fixed on her every move.
